notes:
I can't give you notes on Psalm 107:23–43 yet, because I wasn't able to read any of the sources.

I tried to open five pages at once: the Enduring Word commentary on Psalm 107, Bible Hub's commentary page for 107:23 (which covers Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary), Precept Austin, Augustine's exposition on New Advent and the NET Bible notes. The pages came back in an unexpected format and my script crashed before it printed anything. When I tried again to see what had come back, the tool told me I had used up my code runs for this turn. That tool is the only way I can search or open pages, so I couldn't go further.

You asked me to report only what the pages say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written anything, not even the traditional reading of each verse, which would have to come from memory.

If you ask me to try again in a new message, I'll start with those five pages and then read further for:
- **The traditional reading of each verse:** the same commentaries, plus StudyLight (Gill, Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*).
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** each tradition's own teachers, such as Wesley's notes, Spurgeon and Calvin. Likely places are vv. 23–30 (the storm, and whether it points to Jesus calming the sea) and vv. 33–34 and 40 (God's judgement and his sovereignty).
- **Catholic and Orthodox readings:** Augustine on New Advent (he numbers this Psalm 106) and OCA material.
- **Modern scholarship:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey.
- **Debated popular teaching:** whether vv. 35–38 are used in prosperity teaching, written up only if a page on the allowed sites actually discusses it.

The finished notes will be verse by verse ("v. 23: …"), with a URL after each point.
